newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom to trial Internet toll service.
newsitem.headline: Telecom to trial Internet toll service.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand is about to start trials of an internet-based phone service which will undercut its existing long-distance services, Infotech Weekly reported on Monday.
Internet-based telephony allows phone users to make calls from one telephone to another, but calls travel through the internet global computer network instead of through normal toll lines.
Calls from a personal computer to a telephone and between computers are possible.
Telecom internet service general manager Chris Tyler says the service will be offered through Telecom's Xtra internet company.
Trials involving about 400 Xtra customers will start in about two weeks, offering calls to Britain, the United States and Australia. Details are being finalised to add a further seven countries.
Tyler says eventually the service will be offered to anyone and will include national toll calls and calls to all international destinations.
He says that pricing for the service has not been decided, but initial rates will be competitive with callback rates. Calls will be added to customers' monthly telephone bills.
Callback companies offer New Zealanders access to American telephone networks to make international calls, sometimes at less than half the price of Telecom's peak rates.
Auckland-based internet company Voyager recently announced pricing for its proposed internet telephone service with discounts of 50 percent on Telecom's charges.
Users of Xtra's service will have to dial a special number, and then key in their identification number and the phone number they wish to call.
Internet-based calls will lead to two competing telephone services sold by Telecom, Tyler says.

"Consumers will be able to choose which service they want to make calls with a price differential reflecting the fact that internet telephony won't have the same voice quality as standard telephony and will not be direct dial."
Telecom spokesman Quentin Bright says the impact of internet telephony on the company's toll services will not be immediately apparent but the company expects it to be a big growth area.

Observers say Telecom customers will choose standard tolls services over internet telephony due to better quality, but over time internet quality should improve, and internet telephony could bite into Telecom's national and international toll revenues.

In the last full year ending March 31, 1996, international calls brought in $492.5 million and national toll calls $549.4 million, together making up 33 per cent of Telecom's total operating revenue of $3.19 billion.

Tyler says there are no targets for the percentage of total toll calls delivered through the internet, but he has "bullish" predictions for the growth in internet-based telephone usage. He says internet telephony will be priced to be profitable immediately on a per call basis.

As well as Voyager's internet phone service, Xtra is likely to face competition from many other New Zealand-based internet companies who are looking to launch similar services in the near future, including Wellington-based Actrix networks and Auckland-based Internet Group and Internet Prolink.
Clear Communications has no immediate plans to introduce an internet telephony service but is looking at it for the future.
"My major concern is that call quality is not there yet," group manager of strategic development Craig Holmes says.
It's doubtful international calls will be clear enough when the internet becomes congested, he says.
Internet telephony is only another element causing downward pressure on toll call revenues for phone companies.
"Carriage of bits on a network will become a marginal activity and what we have to do is offer more than just tolls."
-- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
